Quantum Algorithmic Primitives Atlas

A card catalogue of the quantum algorithmic toolkit. Each card is one primitive, an abstract object with a contract in five places, the same for every kind: what it needs (access, promise) and what it guarantees (output, error or, for an architecture, expressivity, and cost). The card records its defining papers, variants, current status and limits, and the hooks that connect it to hardware, to other primitives, to error correction and to verification. Named algorithms and problems are not cards; they are compositions of cards. Edited by Elham Kashefi (Quantum Software Lab, University of Edinburgh; LIP6, Sorbonne Université and CNRS). Compiled with AI agents from the sources listed under About, tested against 2439 items from eight independent corpora, and independently reviewed. Unknowns are marked "?".

Select a card to open its contract, its variants, the papers it rests on and its partners on the composition map. Every arXiv number and DOI opens the paper. Each card has its own link, shown at the top of the card, so it can be sent on its own.

Compiled with AI agents under a written evidence standard and reviewed; the engine notes are AI-generated research notes that no human expert has yet checked.
